objective: Take up PROCESS-CHAIN-20261108-001's direction 1, relayed by the coordinator on 2026-11-08 (G5 with G1; challenges A34): in 195 chains of three rings the far contact binds the end rings at some lags of the eventual cycle but not at every lag. Decide whether that intermittent composition is native: whether its lags are fixed by the chain's own dynamics (composition exactly where the far ring's influence arrives, and only where both contacts bind), and whether it survives transport to the other declared ring sizes; prove the linear case and the strobing reduction.
status: Complete 2026-11-08: intermittent composition is persistent composition of a strobed chain whose phase the chain does not fix; linear chains compose exactly at the arrival of both ends' influence (proved); of 7,040 chains 244 compose at recurring lags and in 92, every one with an affine rule (15, 170, 60, 90, 105, 150), the chain singles out its composing lags, never with a nonlinear rule; one size past the same (24 of 112). A34 confirmed for the gate. Recommendation: Research directions (a middle ring that carries without cancelling on affine chains; the pulse law).
stop_rule: Stop when the linear arrival law and the strobing reduction are proved and the three frozen hypotheses (arrival, coexistence with both contacts, transport across sizes) are decided on the declared chains, or an obstruction is found and explained.
title: Intermittent networks across time: native only on affine substrates
